card.title: 4TP
card.text: Destroy this unit after it attacks the enemy HQ.
card.flavorText: The 4TP (also designated PZInż. 140) was a Polish light reconnaissance tank prototype developed in the mid-1930s as part of the efforts to modernize the country’s armored forces. The tank was designed by engineer Edward Habich at Państwowe Zakłady Inżynierii (PZInż) and his goal was to replace outdated TK-3 and TKS tankettes with a more capable vehicle featuring a rotating turret and enhanced firepower. It was inspired by British Vickers-Carden-Loyd designs, but incorporated Polish innovations such as a torsion bar suspension, a domestically built 95-horsepower PZInż. 425 engine, and a reversible periscope. With a top speed of 55 km/h and a range of 450 km, it was agile and suited for reconnaissance, despite its thin armor (8 to 17 mm) and weak proposed armament: a 20 mm autocannon and a 7.92 mm machine gun. The prototype underwent extensive trials from 1937 to 1939, covering over 4,300 km without major mechanical failures, proving its reliability. Despite plans to produce 480 units for infantry divisions and motorized brigades, the project was canceled in 1939.
